title: QEMU SIGKILL recovery never frees an unverified device
blocker: A standalone durable journal/FSM now proves fail-closed reconciliation after SIGKILL of a Python owner proxy, but there is no production pidfd/systemd-scope identity, kernel-owner reconciliation, verified DMA/IRQ teardown, release reset, or whole-bundle recovery workflow wired to a real QEMU assignment.
assertions: QEMU death is identified by a non-reusable process identity rather than a PID-only check
process absence alone never proves that VFIO ownership, DMA or IRQ state is clean
reconcile releases the bundle only after current-generation cleanup and clean-state evidence are committed
unknown kernel ownership, stale generation, reset failure or missing evidence retains the whole bundle in quarantine
